# archestra_guardrails_policy (Resource)

The text of the organization's guardrails policy. The organization always has one policy: creating this resource replaces its text, and destroying the resource leaves the text as it is. This resource owns the whole text, so do not combine it with `archestra_openappa_battery_install`, which edits the same policy. Requires OpenAPPA guardrails to be enabled.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Keep the organization's guardrails policy in Git. Start from the current
# text under Settings → Guardrails, save it next to this file, and edit it
# there. This resource owns the whole text: manage battery installs in the
# file's `include` list rather than with archestra_openappa_battery_install.
resource "archestra_guardrails_policy" "this" {
  content = file("${path.module}/guardrails-policy.toml")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `content` (String) Policy text. It is validated before it is saved.

### Read-Only

- `content_hash` (String) Hash of the saved policy text.
- `id` (String) Organization ID.
- `revision` (Number) Revision of the saved policy.
- `updated_at` (String) Time the revision was saved.
- `updated_by` (String) ID of the user who saved the revision.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import archestra_guardrails_policy.this <organization id>
```
